items.headline: Council agenda: LinkedIn campus development agreement amendment, second reading
items.summary: The October 27 City Council agenda listed the second reading of an amendment to LinkedIn's development agreement covering 700-810 East Middlefield Road and 1100-1200 Maude Avenue. A second reading is typically the final step in adopting an ordinance.

items.headline: Council agenda: tax-exempt bonds for multifamily housing at 334 San Antonio Road
items.summary: The October 27 City Council agenda included an item on tax-exempt bond financing for a multi-family housing project at 334 San Antonio Road.

items.headline: Council agenda: design concept for Highway 237 and Middlefield interchange
items.summary: The October 27 City Council agenda listed the design concept for State Route 237 and Middlefield Road Interchange Improvements (Project 19-65). The same agenda also covered pre-qualifying bidders and subcontractors for the Public Safety Building (Project 20-49).

items.headline: Council closed session on City Attorney appointment and pay negotiations
items.summary: The October 27 closed session agenda listed a public employee appointment for the City Attorney position. It also listed a labor negotiator conference regarding the City Attorney, who is an unrepresented employee.

items.headline: 40 townhomes proposed at 1380 & 1400 W. Campbell Avenue
items.summary: The October 27 Planning Commission agenda listed a public hearing on Madrone Ventures' plan for six three-story townhome buildings with 40 units, plus a subdivision map. The plan includes removing existing street trees along W. Campbell Avenue. Staff recommended approval, and the project is reviewed under the rules in effect when its May 2025 preliminary application was filed, under the Housing Crisis Act.

items.headline: Campbell proposes replacement-housing rules for demolitions
items.summary: The October 27 Planning Commission agenda listed a hearing on a Replacement Housing and Demolition Control Ordinance. It would set replacement-unit requirements and demolition controls under the state Housing Crisis Act and the city's Housing Element. Staff recommended that the commission send it to the City Council, tentatively set for December 1, 2026.

items.headline: Home Depot on E. Hamilton Avenue gets a compliance review
items.summary: The October 27 Planning Commission agenda listed a public hearing reviewing operations of the Home Depot hardware store and garden center at 480 E. Hamilton Avenue. Staff's recommended action was to receive a report documenting substantial compliance with the permit's conditions of approval.

items.headline: Sunnyvale parking rules rewrite listed with continuance request to Nov. 9
items.summary: The Oct. 26 Planning Commission agenda listed a proposed citywide ordinance to repeal and replace the residential off-street parking chapter (19.46) of the zoning code. It would also amend the Downtown, Lawrence Station, and El Camino Real specific plan chapters and the Dual Urban Opportunity Housing chapter. The agenda carried a request to continue the item to Nov. 9, 2026, and the commission's recommendation would go to the City Council.
